Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Quickdraw sessions and social UI

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Replay Quickdraw starts at a scene-authored menu. Enter a name and choose Solo, Host, Join or Watch. Address and port are editable before connection. Host opens a waiting duel; the first connected player is the match leader and can Start. Gameplay remains stationary until that command is accepted. Solo starts immediately. Scripted RQ_ROLE launches retain automatic play, and the existing credential-based Room launches still open automatically unless RQ_AUTO=0.

Enter focuses chat; Escape releases focus and preserves the draft. Typing captures movement, drone steering, firing, dash, lob and purchase input while networking and simulation keep running. Submitted text is displayed literally. Observer chat waits for negotiated display-name support before enabling submission, so the selected label is included without changing the observer's admitted identity or seat zero.

Tab shows the authoritative scoreboard: player name, kills, deaths, gold and measured round-trip time. Departed rows remain until their seat is reused. Leave closes the session and returns to the menu. Rejoining with the retained identity restores the same seat and existing scores; chat history is supplied by the active authority.

Player names, waiting/started state and the manual-start policy are values inside World. Names are declared through validated seat-owned actions. Start is rejected for anyone other than the current first connected player, or after play has begun. Existing movement, damage, hit-query, respawn, projectile, shop and score rules are unchanged once the duel starts.

Normal native play retains a local identity and display name using the shared profile helpers. Explicit RQ_TOKEN, a bot, or RQ_PERSIST=0 bypasses these local preferences for tests. RQ_PROFILE selects an alternate identity path; the name uses that path plus .name. Corrupt data is preserved and joining reports the failure. These preferences are distinct from game checkpoints and Room credentials. Browser identity/name persistence and service-backed party invitations use the shared Party integration. Public deployment remains separate work.

Names, start policy, and their actions use experimental content ID 0x52515549434b4432 (D2) because they change the complete state/action schema. D1 peers and archives are intentionally incompatible; there is no implicit old-save conversion. Original Kit Quickdraw remains separately runnable with its original content and protocol. Host migration still requires a compatible prepared checkpoint; changing this UI does not waive lease, rollback-window or admission rules.

The native UI fixture is tests/replay_quickdraw_ui/run.sh. It drives real menu buttons and three processes, tests start authorization and input capture, verifies literal and named observer chat, produces a real kill for nonzero scoreboard rows, and leaves/rejoins without resetting scores. Separate regression runners retain the existing historical/live A/B, predicted lob and combat migration checks.

This is a session/UI parity increment, not full Quickdraw completion. Broader combat feedback review, public/browser/Steam paths, measurements and human visual/play-feel review remain in the full roadmap.

Native file saves provide Save/F5 and Resume solo/host. They preserve a complete authority checkpoint and require its host identity; coordinated Room recovery remains a separate path.
